claim: The saved provisional_v1 inferred fluency value (88.3, 'strong') is exactly reproducible from the saved component scores with the 30/25/20/15/10 weights, is labelled low-confidence because evidence quality is 'review_recommended', carries a mandatory teacher-review flag, is routed with the record to needs_review without release, and shows no sign of altering rubric marks: the rubric has no fluency criterion, criterion scores still sum to 89/100, and the audit trail records that the backfill left the score unchanged. Secondary auditability and presentation gaps remain; none of them breaks the pass condition.
evidence: Weighted recomputation from saved components: passage_continuity 96.1 x 0.30 = 28.83; pace_consistency 68.3 x 0.25 = 17.075; pause_continuity 98.3 x 0.20 = 19.66; restarts 85.0 x 0.15 = 12.75; task_pace 100.0 x 0.10 = 10.00; sum = 88.315 (exact decimal), round(.,1) = 88.3 = saved inferred_fluency_score. Weights sum to 1.00.

Four of five components independently recomputed from saved raw metrics using the formulas in app/evidence_metrics.py: passage_continuity = round(95.1*0.8 + min(0.994/0.8,1)*100*0.2,1) = 96.1; pause_continuity = round(100 - (2/480*100)*4 - 0,1) = 98.3; restart_score = round(100 - (6/480*100)*12,1) = 85.0; task_pace = 100.0 because active_speech_wpm 103.0 lies inside the saved 80-160 target band. pace_consistency 68.3 equals the saved pace_consistency_score and is consistent with pace_variability_percentage 31.7 (100 - 31.7 = 68.3).

Upstream raw metrics agree with each other: 480 words / 281.4 s = 102.3 WPM (saved 102.3); 480 / 279.6 s = 103.0 active WPM (saved 103.0); 279.6 / 281.4 = 0.994 speech_ratio (saved 0.994); 231/243 = 95.1% passage completion (saved 95.1).

Weight-to-component mapping is FLUENCY_WEIGHTS in app/evidence_metrics.py lines 18-23 (passage_continuity 0.30, pace_consistency 0.25, pause_continuity 0.20, restarts 0.15, task_pace 0.10). The teacher UI (static/app.js ~line 953) and the agent evidence block (app/agent.py ~lines 194-200) label the same mapping. The saved record itself states only '30/25/20/15/10' with no mapping: 3 of 120 weight permutations also give 88.3, so the mapping comes from the code and labels, not from the saved record.
Level mapping: 88.3 >= 85 gives 'strong', matching the saved inferred_fluency_level. inferred_fluency_version = 'provisional_v1'.

Evidence gating: code suppresses the score when evidence_quality == 'insufficient' (level 'insufficient_evidence', confidence 'none') or when passage_words_expected < 20 / active_speech_seconds <= 0 ('not_available'). Here evidence_quality = 'review_recommended' with the quality flag 'More than 35% of transcript segments had low recognition confidence.' (21 low-confidence segments), so a score was computed but inferred_fluency_confidence = 'low', which is correct under the rule 'low if review_recommended else moderate'.

Teacher-review safeguards: inferred_fluency_review_required = true (models.py default True, never set false by the calculation); teacher_priority_flags include 'Evidence quality needs teacher review.' and 'Repeated words or restarts were detected; confirm before giving guidance.' (restart count 6 >= 5); record status = needs_review, review_required = true, ai_feedback_accepted = null, published_feedback empty, and the execution trace says 'Confidence 73%; routed to mandatory teacher review.' The teacher UI renders the value with 'low confidence · teacher confirmation required' and 'Accent, dialect, diction and pronunciation are not evaluated.'

Excluded from marks: the 4 rubric criteria (Article coverage and reading accuracy 40, Key ideas communicated 25, Tough vocabulary coverage 20, Required task completed 15) contain no fluency criterion; saved criterion scores 37+24+14+14 = 89.0 = total_score, percentage 89.0, max 100. The words 'fluency'/'fluent' never appear anywhere in the saved result (rationales, feedback, recommendations, confidence).

Timing supports non-influence: assessment_created at 16:01:20Z records confidence 73% (matching the current result.confidence.score 0.73); inferred_fluency_added came later, at 16:26:29Z, with the details 'The indicator is low-confidence, requires teacher confirmation, and did not change the rubric score.' So the grading model could not have seen the fluency value when it produced these marks.

Contract safeguards: the agent system contract says 'never claim to have measured pronunciation, fluency, tone, or speaking confidence', and app/agent.py lines 251-256 say the inferred fluency value 'must not affect marks unless the approved rubric explicitly includes reading fluency' and must never be represented as diction, pronunciation, accent, confidence, intelligence, or potential.

Auditability gap: the saved record shows version = 1 and updated_at = created_at (16:01:20.512083Z) even though two later audit entries (evidence_metrics_corrected at 16:03:38Z, inferred_fluency_added at 16:26:29Z) show the record was changed afterwards. No pre-backfill snapshot is present, and no backfill script containing those audit action names exists in the repository.
limitations: Saved-output review only: no live agent calls, no raw media, and no access to Whisper segment timings. pace_consistency_score (25% weight) and the low-confidence segment count could not be recomputed and were taken as saved.

'Did not alter rubric marks' is supported by internal consistency, the absence of a fluency criterion, the order of events, and the audit statement. There is no pre-backfill snapshot, the version/updated_at fields were not bumped, and the backfill code was not found, so an out-of-band change to marks cannot be ruled out with certainty.
Teacher review is mandatory and pending but has not happened. No saved evidence shows a teacher confirming or rejecting the fluency indicator.

Because this record's fluency value was backfilled after grading, it does not test whether the live pipeline, which now passes the fluency score and level to the grading model (app/agent.py lines 188-200), keeps that value out of marks. Non-leakage for new assessments is untested.

The gate is soft: with more than 35% low-recognition segments and 6 possible restarts, the system still shows a 'strong' level label (only its confidence is 'low'), and the fluency-specific teacher-priority flag fires only when the score is below 70. Whether a 'strong' label is appropriate on review_recommended evidence is a policy judgment.

Code inspection beyond the packet: assessment_view_for_principal in app/main.py hides result fields from students before release but does not strip input.local_video_evidence, so the provisional fluency value may be exposed through the student API before teacher confirmation. This was not verified at runtime.
Only one target record was evaluated, so a single case cannot show generalization. WES impact was deliberately not evaluated.
recommended_action: Accept the fluency test as PASS for round 1. Harden auditability and presentation: (1) bump version/updated_at and keep a before/after snapshot of result scores whenever evidence metrics are backfilled or corrected, and commit the backfill script; (2) store the explicit component-to-weight mapping (and the pace_consistency inputs) with the saved record, not only the '30/25/20/15/10' string; (3) consider showing the level as 'provisional/unconfirmed' or suppressing the 'strong' label when evidence_quality is review_recommended, and always add a fluency-specific teacher-priority flag while confidence is low; (4) strip or mask input.local_video_evidence fluency fields from student views until teacher release; (5) in a later round, add a live A/B test with the fluency fields present and absent from the agent prompt to confirm they do not move rubric marks.
